items.title: Broadneck · ox-like working animal
items.description: A proposed ox-like working animal for farms and roads beyond the salt plains. Its compact mass, spreading feet and broad shoulders support a practical harness; the name and exact regional distribution remain open.
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one original Breachline ANIMAL REFERENCE SHEET, landscape 1536x1024, showing the SAME new ox-like working animal in coherent repeated views. Warm pale plain ground, neutral light, traditional oil/acrylic concept painting with deliberate selective brushwork, matte animal materials. No text, numbering, border or watermark.
The user wants an everyday sturdy ox-like working animal for farms and roads in regions other than the salt plains. Make a quiet, appealing, patient heavy-bodied living herbivore, around an adult person's shoulder height at its withers, with four powerful legs, a deep broad chest and muscular short neck, a slightly sloping back and compact sturdy hindquarters. Its recognisable ox-like weight and strength are important, but this is original fantasy wildlife, not a normal ox with ornamental accessories. A broad elongated blunt soft-lipped grazing head, calm lateral eyes, small sideways ears; a pair of thick low horn roots sweep outward and slightly down close to the skull. No giant weapon horns or frightening mouth. Broad feet have three short blunt weight-bearing keratin toes set into fleshy pads, able to spread on soft soil. The animal's shoulders and neck have close-set layered coarse chestnut bristles, thinning into warm slate-grey leathery hide across the deep flanks; the transitions follow its muscle masses. A short heavy tail ends in a simple brush. Coherent organic anatomy; no throat combs, dorsal sacks, fungus, extra limbs, plates glued to a cow or random frills.
LAYOUT: a large unobstructed three-quarter standing view occupying the left half, all four legs and entire head/tail visible; on upper right a clean side profile of the same animal walking without gear; lower right a smaller front-three-quarter working view with a simple padded shoulder collar and two modest balanced woven panniers attached by a practical leather-and-wood pack frame over the ribs, free of the spine and foreleg movement. No cart, reins tied around the throat, decorative tack or excess straps. One small neutral adult human silhouette beside the main view establishes working-animal scale. Show the anatomical body clearly; the harness view is only one practical handling proposal. Compact powerful stance, believable contact and support, friendly sober presence rather than pet cuteness. Keep the same head, toes, covering pattern and proportions in all three views.
items.visual_check: Inspected generated image: selected identity and requested scene retained, connected anatomy and readable paint; OX1 is a new proposed design.

Powerful living predator, a patient closed mouth, no snarl, fangs, attack, prey, harness or person. An economical natural scene, a few clear rock masses rather than busy repeated texture.

items.title: Veilwing · aligned-wing anatomy study
items.description: The approved anatomy study establishes the aligned, matching wing pair in its large overhead view. Supporting angle views preserve the slender body, translucent sails and trailing ribbons; giant scale remains in force.
items.creator_request: lets do an anatomy study of this guy real quick. the wing facing us has an orientation that doesnt quite make sense. align the wings in study
items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / creature anatomy reference. Make a clear THREE-VIEW ANATOMY STUDY of the same Veilwing from attached references, 1536x1024 landscape on plain warm ivory. Image 1 preserves creature identity, colour and huge scale, but its near wing is incorrectly oriented: DO NOT repeat that pose. Image 2 supplies ancestral identity ONLY in cell 5 BOTTOM MIDDLE. This is an anatomical clarification, not a new animal or a variant lineup.
Preserve slender elongated pointed head and torso, delicate paired head feelers, translucent cream/amber/lavender sail surfaces with mottled vein structure, lobed trailing edges and long rear ribbon streamers. ONE bilaterally matched pair of broad sail-wings. Left and right wing roots attach at the SAME longitudinal station on opposite sides of the torso. Both leading edges face toward the head, both lobed trailing edges sweep toward the tail. Both wings have the SAME shape, lobe arrangement and anatomical orientation mirrored left-to-right. They spread into the SAME shallow flight plane. Do not put one wing facing forward or down the body's length while the other faces sideways. Continuous membrane lobes are parts of the same sail, not extra wing pairs.
LAYOUT: Large true OVERHEAD/DORSAL view across the left two-thirds of the sheet, head pointing toward top of page, tail ribbons toward bottom. No roll or foreshortening: full left and right sails extend symmetrically sideways, visibly mirrored, roots and continuous leading edges easy to trace. Upper right: smaller exact HEAD-ON view, slender head and torso centered between the matched wings, both in equal shallow dihedral, both roots at equal height, showing their shared plane. Lower right: exact SIDE PROFILE of the same anatomy, head pointing left; near and far matched wings overlap in projection rather than becoming different shapes. All three views depict the SAME number of wing elements, same root positions, same body proportions. Keep each whole view inside its own space with clear margins, no overlap.
Omit leather harness in this anatomy-only sheet so wing/body connections are unobscured; the established harness direction remains leather over the back with no people aboard, but no tack is needed here. Two minute human scale marks below the side study communicate a truly enormous animal, not a small mount. Neutral even light; measured painterly gouache/oil concept handling with clear structural edges, quiet shading and no scenic setting. No bones, no gore, no invented legs, no second head, no redesign into a bird, butterfly or ordinary ray. No text, letters, labels, diagrams, arrows, borders or watermark.
